title: The Assistant Remembered What My Husband Forgot

core_axes.inciting_disruption: A florist's assistant, by phone, tells Ines alone in her kitchen that 'his office' (assistant Fern Alcott) calls in the anniversary order every year; next morning Fern confirms by phone in the school parking lot that she has written every card, picked every gift and dinner, and booked Margo's medical care for eight years. There is no audience and no affair.
core_axes.the_bind: Nothing external holds her: she still loves the actual man, and Naomi lists what leaving would cost (half the house, no credit for 18 months of unpaid early bookkeeping for Calloway Freight, a principal's social exposure in a small town). So she binds herself with a one-year deadline that has a real divorce consequence.
core_axes.first_irreversible_decision: Ch 4: she hands Whit the six-page list 'EVERYTHING I HAVE BEEN RUNNING', removes Fern from the shared marriage calendar in front of him through three confirmation screens, has already moved Margo's cardiology contact off Fern, and sets one year with a filing with Naomi as the price. Her visible price is giving up her own safety-net role, so nobody covers the dropped tasks.
core_axes.midpoint_reversal: Ch 22-24: Whit nearly forgets Margo's birthday, catches it at 4:40pm, and tells her the truth that he almost forgot, without calling Ines or Fern. Ines then catches herself texting that she had booked the gutter cleaners, Naomi names it as the same overfunctioning habit, and the repair becomes two-sided rather than his alone.
core_axes.rupture_lowest_point: Ch 39-40, nine days before the deadline: Margo falls while the Vance team has flown in unannounced to force a decision. Whit says 'I'm going to send Fern' and stays 90 more minutes to close a three-year renewal. Fern goes out of love for Margo, not for him. Whit arrives at 4:55pm, and in Margo's driveway admits 'I failed the test.'
core_axes.climax_action: Ch 44: a reefer unit fails on the first Berkline load and Roland Vance demands Whit in person. Whit decides overnight, with Ines deliberately giving no advice, to have COO Deborah lead the response and not fly. He invites Ines to his office at about 8am and phones Roland on speaker with her as the only witness, stating the real reason (the anniversary and his mother's fall). Roland laughs and says 'Send Deborah... Happy anniversary.' Whit causes the outcome and Ines witnesses it.
core_axes.repair_mechanism: Self-performed care done badly and repeated, witnessed mostly by Ines and Margo: he attends Lila's concert alone with his phone left in the car, cooks Thanksgiving, burns the chicken at Margo's, sorts Desmond's study himself, and calls the Ashworths. He also arranges Deshawn's rides and tells no one; Ines learns of it by accident. Further acts: the six o'clock phone rule, data entry for her audit, the leave-by-six company policy (witnessed by employees), and promoting Deborah. Client Roland Vance and his wife Cheryl independently notice the change.
core_axes.resolution_epilogue_shape: There is no epilogue. Ch 45: his prepared index-card apology collapses after card seven into a plain 'I let you disappear', and she answers 'I love you' with their first kiss of the year. Ch 46, the anniversary Saturday: a card in his own hand misspelling 'deserve'. Margo hands over Desmond's box of cards. Ines overhears, unseen, Whit confirm Margo's appointment and make himself the contact, a callback to ch 4. They walk out to two cars with no plan.

first_attraction_quote: looking, for all the world, like someone who had shown up somewhere on time because he wanted to be there and not because anyone had told him to. (ch 5, Ines watching from the back row before he sees her)
first_care_quote: carrying a bag from the good Thai place, the one three towns over that I loved and he found mediocre and always ordered from anyway because I loved it. (ch 2, immediately undercut: she wonders whether that too 'had gone out under someone else's name')
opening_first_sentence: The handwriting on the card was wrong.

evidence_notes.source: Full text read: all 46 chapters plus author note (PDF, 168 pp). Drive read_file_content truncated at ch 18 (~p.80 of 168), so the PDF was downloaded with download_file_content and extracted with pdftotext; every chapter was read in full.
evidence_notes.pen_name: Printed 'Veyra Thornwyck'; copyright page names Michael A Smith. Cover subtitle: 'A Workaholic CEO Neglected Wife Grovel Romance'.
evidence_notes.workplace_function: The workplace is the husband's company, Calloway Freight: logistics, 110 staff, founded by his late father Desmond with six trucks. It is not a coworker romance, and Ines never works there (except 18 months of unpaid early bookkeeping, mentioned once). It does three jobs. (1) It is the instrument of the harm: executive assistant Fern runs the marriage as office logistics, and Whit tries to replace her with a hired 'family operations coordinator' (Yvette, ch 10-11). (2) The Vance/Berkline account (28% of volume, 20-25 layoffs at stake) is the recurring pressure that produces each test: the dizzy spell where he texts Ines (ch 14), the relapse at the hospital (ch 39-40), and the reefer-failure climax (ch 43-44). (3) It is where repair becomes structural: he delegates real work to COO Deborah (the right delegation replacing the wrong one), sets a leave-by-six policy (ch 30), and the client Roland Vance and his wife act as outside witnesses that the change is real (ch 19, 36). Ines's own school is a mirror plot, not a containment: Denise Ferreira, the 'competent child' who carries her household, and Deshawn Ruiz. Priscilla Ochoa is her confidante there.
evidence_notes.climax_staging: The book explicitly stages against a public climax: 'past the glassed-in conference room where I had pictured... a long table, a row of faces, an audience... The conference room was dark.' Venue: Whit's office, blinds down, about 8am, a half-empty building with a custodian's floor buffer. The phone is on speaker on the desk. The only people present are Ines (invited by him) and Roland's voice. No documents are produced; the act is the call itself. Roland's laugh settles the business stakes. The marriage verdict is Ines's own and is spoken in ch 45 at the kitchen island ('I love you' and a kiss), so the relational climax is a separate private scene two days later. The deadline is never formally declared 'passed' in words.
evidence_notes.midpoint_note: Midpoint judged at ch 22-24 of 46: the honest late birthday, then the heroine's own overfunctioning exposed. The Vance dinner (ch 19) is the first point where the workplace sees the change.
evidence_notes.heroine_goal_note: Her goal is bound up with the partner: a truthful verdict rather than a career or asset goal. No external goal of hers is threatened.
evidence_notes.ending_final_paragraph: We walked out the back door together, into an ordinary Saturday afternoon, toward two separate cars, in no hurry, for once, to decide which one to take.
evidence_notes.ending_image_secondary: callback_to_opening (keys from ch 1, a card read at the same island, the contact-on-file change mirroring ch 4)
evidence_notes.inciting_secondary: omission (eight years of delegated care) is the underlying harm, and discovery is the event.
evidence_notes.continuity_flags: Ch 44 says 'my tenth wedding anniversary' but the book opens on the tenth and ends on the eleventh. Ages at the wedding are given as 29/32 (ch 3) and 29/31 (ch 38); Whit is said to be 46 (ch 12). Fern is 26 at the start of eight years but '29' at Desmond's death three years ago. Seasons drift: 'that spring' is used for November-January events, and Camille says 'eight months in' at about week 7. Margo's 'fall' on the porch steps is referred back to, but ch 14 was a dizzy spell. Ch 34 says Whit watched his father '38 years'.
evidence_notes.heat: No sex on the page. The first kiss of the year is deliberately withheld (ch 17 near-kiss interrupted by a phone he lets ring) until ch 45.
